The Beaumont parties point out that a portion of Orange County, Tex., which was found to be commercially a part of Beaumont in a prior proceeding was omitted from the Beaumont commercial zone described in the proposed amended section 1048.1 of the regulations. The Lake Charles parties complain that a portion of Calcasieu Parish, La., which is within the presently defined zone is omitted from the zone by the redefinition contained in the proposed amended section 1048.4.
Arguments opposing zone expansion by shipper, local interests, State agencies, and individuals. - These parties fear that the proposed action may undermine the financial stability of the small, short-haul carriers causing a deterioration of the good service they are presently receiving. They fear that rates will increase particularly for small shippers, and that exempt carriers will cause theft, safety, and claims handling problems. Some cities fear that zone expansion will encourage business and industry to relocate in the suburbs, further aggravating the problems of urban decay, eroding tax bases, and increasing inner city unemployment. Other parties fear that zone expansion will encourage urban sprawl and frustrate planned development in the suburbs.
